AfterRoomEntered.maps_to: on_combat_start (ember_tea.py:28-34) -- the sim moves the effect from the room-entry hook to the BeforeCombatStart slot
AfterRoomEntered.rationale: EmberTea.cs:57-65 fires on AfterRoomEntered filtered to `room is CombatRoom`, applies StrengthPower at DynamicVars.Strength.BaseValue (2, EmberTea.cs:32 PowerVar<StrengthPower>(2m), no AscensionHelper branch in the file) and decrements CombatsLeft. The sim's on_combat_start does the same three things in the same order with the same numbers (ember_tea.py:29-34), and the effect count matches exactly: executed (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b05.py ember-order) five consecutive combats each give Strength 2 with combats_left 5->0, and combats 6 and 7 give 0 with is_used_up True. The SLOT differs -- see guard G1 -- but the observable a player or replay sees is the same, so this is a divergence rather than a gap; the ordering risk is verdicted on its own guard entry.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): C#'s AfterRoomEntered runs strictly BEFORE every BeforeCombatStart listener; the sim's on_combat_start runs interleaved with them in relic-registration order
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CombatRoom.cs:224-228 calls CombatManager.SetUpCombat and then Hook.AfterRoomEntered; Hook.BeforeCombatStart is only reached later, from CombatManager.StartCombatInternal (CombatManager.cs:403, after IsInProgress is set at :402). So in C# the +2 Strength is on the player before ANY BeforeCombatStart listener runs. The sim registers relics in run order (combat.py:158-159) and dispatches on_combat_start over that flat list, so Ember Tea's Strength lands before some combat-start effects and after others depending on the order the relics were picked up -- the audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json G2 listener-order shape at this relic's site. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b05.py ember-order): 23 ported relics implement on_combat_start; 6 mention Strength (ember_tea, girya, philosophers_stone, sling_of_courage, sword_of_jade, vajra) and every one of the six only APPLIES it through PowerCmd.apply / StrengthCmd.apply -- Strength addition commutes, so the totals agree. An AST scan of EVERY on_combat_start body anywhere under sts2_rl/ finds ZERO that read a power at all (no powers.get / get_power), so nothing in the window can observe the difference. Porting a BeforeCombatStart effect that READS the player's Strength -- a 'gain Block equal to your Strength' relic is the obvious shape -- makes it live. Rule 7: CombatRoom.cs, CombatManager.cs, combat.py and the five sibling relic files are unhashed here.

guards.what: N1: `!IsUsedUp && room is CombatRoom` (EmberTea.cs:59) vs the sim's `if self.is_used_up: return` in a combat-only hook (ember_tea.py:29-30)
guards.rationale: The IsUsedUp half is mirrored exactly. The `room is CombatRoom` half is structurally satisfied: on_combat_start is a combat hook, dispatched only when a CombatState exists, so the sim cannot fire it in a rest site or shop. Note that C# filters on the ROOM being a combat room, not on a combat existing -- CombatRoom.cs:203 shows a room whose ShouldCreateCombat is false still reaches :228, so a pre-finished combat room would tick a charge in C# and not in the sim. The sim has no pre-finished-combat concept (combats are created by RunState.create_combat when the room resolves), so that half is unreachable rather than divergent.

guards.what: N2: `_combatsLeft = 5` (EmberTea.cs:19) is instance state that C# persists with [SavedProperty] (EmberTea.cs:37-38) and the sim keeps as a plain instance field (ember_tea.py:20-22) with NO combat-boundary reset
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md bug class 13 requires the trace, and here the missing reset is CORRECT: the counter is per-RUN on both sides. C# gives it no BeforeCombatStart or AfterCombatEnd reset either (the file's only other override is AfterRoomEntered) and marks it [SavedProperty] so it survives a save/load. The sim's relic instance lives on RunState.relics and is re-attached to each new CombatState, which is exactly the persistence the counter needs -- executed above: 5 -> 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0 across five separate CombatState constructions with the same instance. This relic is in .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md sweep A's 'never reset at a combat boundary' bucket for that reason and is cleared here.

guards.what: N3: PowerCmd.Apply<StrengthPower>(new ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext(), Owner.Creature, 2, null, null) (EmberTea.cs:62) -- applier and cardSource both null -- vs StrengthCmd.apply(hooks, player, 2) (ember_tea.py:33)
guards.rationale: StrengthCmd.apply (cmds.py:349-361) runs hooks.modify_strength_given and then PowerCmd.apply with no applier and no card, matching both nulls. Checked deliberately for the same reason relic/belt_buckle's N3 was: an applier-carrying application would be a new relic/unsettling_lamp interaction (its doubling requires `applier is self.player`). Both sides pass none, so no such interaction exists -- and the amount is positive, so the Lamp's Debuff typing excludes it anyway. ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext is multiplayer plumbing (a context that throws if a choice is required), noted in the mapping rather than verdicted as a divergence per the shared contract's scope section. Rule 7: cmds.py is unhashed here.

guards.what: N4: DynamicVars.Strength.BaseValue (EmberTea.cs:62) vs DisplayAmount's Math.Max(0, CombatsLeft) (EmberTea.cs:27) -- the BaseValue/IntValue asymmetry
guards.rationale: The applied amount reads BaseValue of PowerVar<StrengthPower>(2m) (EmberTea.cs:32) = 2 with no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so STRENGTH = 2 and COMBATS = 5 (ember_tea.py:17-18) are the pinned non-ascension values. The Math.Max(0, ...) clamp exists only so the counter cannot display negative; CombatsLeft never goes below 0 because line 59 bails once IsUsedUp.
